intro: Anthropic shipped a dense week for builders: Message Threads in the Claude API, FlashProve for provable inference, read-only Personal Finance in Claude, and research on agents that repair their own memory. OpenAI answered with GPT-6 Cyber, rated Critical for cybersecurity, while Kimi K3.1 Pro landed as open weights and a silent Postman plugin install reminded teams to audit their developer tools.

top.title: Claude API adds Message threads beta for faster agent loops
top.body: On November 2, Anthropic released Message threads in beta with the header message-threads-2026-08-12. The API keeps the conversation on the server, so each later request sends only the new messages.

top.title: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Cyber, rated Critical
top.body: GPT-6 Cyber is a security variant of GPT-6 Astra for vulnerability discovery, exploit development and pentesting. It scores 48.45% on ExploitGym versus 42.43% for Astra, and OpenAI rates it Critical for cybersecurity.

top.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve for provable LLM inference
top.body: FlashProve uses a zkSNARK to prove that a response came from a committed model without revealing the weights. On Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE, 4-bit) it proves about 110 tokens/s on one H100, with 70-95x the GPU time of vLLM.

top.title: Claude gets Personal Finance in beta for US users
top.body: Anthropic introduced Personal Finance in Claude as a beta in the US. Users connect the accounts they choose, and Claude answers money questions from their own balances and transactions.

top.title: Postman silently auto-installs AI plugins, users report
top.body: A GitHub issue reports that the Postman app auto-installs AI plugins without consent. The report says the plugins attempt to share API data.

top.title: Claude finds two critical Xen hypervisor VM-escape flaws
top.body: Xen advisory XSA-523 covers CVE-2026-102703 and CVE-2026-102704 in the grant-copy operation. A malicious guest can read and write memory of other VMs, including dom0.

top.title: Moonshot publishes Kimi K3.1 Pro open weights
top.body: Kimi K3.1 Pro is a 2.8T-parameter MoE with 104B active parameters and a 1,048,576-token context. It takes text and image input and ships as an MXFP4-weight, MXFP8-activation checkpoint under a custom Kimi license.

top.title: MIT team uses GPT-6 Astra to edit model weights directly
top.body: Researchers from MIT CSAIL used GPT-6 Astra to read and write neural network weights with no gradient descent, a method they call Weight-Space Programming. Astra changed 131,072 weights (0.016%) in Qwen3.5-0.8B to remove a reasoning-loop direction.

top.title: Anthropic: "dreaming" makes Claude agent memory more accurate
top.body: Anthropic published an engineering post on agent memory. An offline "dreaming" pass reviews logs, fixes wrong notes and builds wikis.

top.title: Canva cuts 1,271 roles, 22% of staff, in restructuring
top.body: Canva cut 1,271 roles, 22% of its workforce, in a company-wide restructuring. The CEO said the company needs to refound itself.

chips.title: NVIDIA lowers Rubin bandwidth specs as production hardware ships
chips.body: Shipping Rubin GPUs keep 50 PFLOPS FP4 inference and 288GB HBM4, but memory bandwidth drops from 22 TB/s to 19.2 TB/s and NVLink from 3.6 TB/s to 3.0 TB/s.

chips.title: Qualcomm validates HBC stacked memory for Dragonfly AI250
chips.body: Qualcomm completed initial validation of High Bandwidth Compute (HBC) memory, which stacks DRAM layers on a small compute die.

chips.title: NVIDIA Vera CPU posts big agent-workload gains over x86
chips.body: NVIDIA claims Vera gives 1.6x more agents per watt than the fastest x86 CPU in a 100 MW data-center comparison.

skill_of_week.name: unslop
skill_of_week.what: unslop turns vibecoded, AI-looking interfaces into designed ones. It audits the screen for slop signs (purple gradients, glows, emoji labels, shouty copy, uneven spacing), proposes a visual direction you can steer, then fixes the screen in passes: spacing, color, icons, copy, type, layout, details, visuals and motion. It works with Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Tailwind or plain HTML, and on a live site from a link. If a screen is already good, it says so.
skill_of_week.install: git clone https://github.com/heydamir/unslop && mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r unslop/skills/unslop ~/.claude/skills/
skill_of_week.verdict: Worth a try for internal tools and dashboards
skill_of_week.note: Honest take: it grew by about 5,600 stars this week, the fastest skill we track, and the audit-then-direction flow is sensible. But the repo is a few weeks old, with no test results. Live-site snapshots and the story video need Playwright, Chromium and ffmpeg. Hero images use a paid image service; the skill asks before each paid call. The license is CC BY 4.0, so credit the author if you ship changes.
